newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore oil products mixed on crude rally.
newsitem.headline: Singapore oil products mixed on crude rally.

text.p: Singapore oil products were mixed on Tuesday with jet fuel and gas oil steady while fuel oil rose following a rally on crude prices as tensions mount in Iraq, traders said.

Swaps November and December gas oil gained 25-40 cents earlier in the day on overnight gains on IPE crude and heating oil to be traded at $30.05 for November. Following two sales by a European major Monday at $29.75 and $30.20 for October 29-Nov 2, the major again offered on Tuesday at $30.50 for Nov 10-14 lifting. Bids were seen from a Japanese trader at $29.90 for Oct 30-Nov 3 and a Singapore trader at $30.10 for Oct 31-Nov 4.

A trader said sellers were staying away and closely watching Saddam Hussein's reaction to the seizure of three nothern Iraq towns by anti-Baghdad Kurdish rebels and the counter-attack launched on Tuesday by pro-Saddam Kurdish militiamen. "But unless the US reacted to any moves by Saddam, the market here will not be overly bullish," one trader said.
India has issued a tender to buy December-arrival gas oil, which closes on October 24.
A US major sold 120,000 barrels of jet fuel at $30 a barrel to a Singapore trader for Oct 30-Nov 3 lifting fob, the same level that a European major sold to the trader on Monday.

India's tender to buy December-arrival kerosene will be issued in a week's time, industry source said. Nepal bought kerosene from Mobil at $249.50 a tonne c+f Indian east coast and gas oil from BP at $232.80.

Fuel oil prices rose $1 a tonne over Monday's levels and was earlier indicated between $121 and $124 for 180-cst lifting end-October. A bid was seen from a major at $120 but offers were unseen. Two cargoes were heard to be distressed. Traders said both cargoes were for October loading ber, one from Singapore and the other from S. Korea. Most traders said supplies remained adequate to meet demand.--Singapore newsroom (+65-870-3084)
